parameters.errorMessage: config.limits.alert_cooldown_minutes must be an integer of 1 or more

parameters.query: SELECT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM inbound_messages WHERE phone = $1 AND received_at > now() - make_interval(mins => $2) AND triage->>'team_alerted' = 'true' AND ($3::text IS DISTINCT FROM 'emergency' OR triage->>'alerted_reason' = 'emergency')) AS alerted
UPDATE inbound_messages SET triage = coalesce(triage, '{}'::jsonb) || jsonb_build_object('team_alerted', true, 'alerted_reason', $2::text) WHERE message_id = $1

parameters.content:
## Notify team
Compose alert (generated from src/nodes/compose-alert.ts) writes a plain-text alert (so patient-written text can't inject markup) in config.team_locale's language and emails config.team_email; a team_locale naming no supported language still sends, in English, with a line saying so. A per-phone cooldown keeps one phone from using up the Gmail daily quota that real emergencies rely on: unless the reason is tool_failure (a system failure the team must always hear about), Check alert cooldown asks whether any of this phone's inbound messages within config.limits.alert_cooldown_minutes is marked team_alerted, and if so returns { ok: true, suppressed: true } without sending. An emergency is held back only by an earlier emergency, so an earlier alert of another kind, such as a question about an unlisted treatment, never keeps a dental emergency from the team; every other reason is held back by any earlier alert. Suppressed means an earlier alert reached the team inside the window, not this one, so a caller must not tell the patient this request was forwarded. Check alert cooldown setting first refuses an alert_cooldown_minutes that isn't an integer of 1 or more, into a Stop and Error the error workflow reports, instead of silently turning the cooldown off; tool_failure alerts skip it and still send. A cooldown check that itself fails sends anyway. After a send, Mark team alerted marks the caller's message_id with team_alerted and the alert's reason as alerted_reason, which the cooldown reads back (callers without a message_id mark nothing), and a failed mark still returns { ok: true }. Returns { ok: true }, or { ok: false, reason: 'email_failed' } when Gmail's error output fires.
